# Relationship, Address, and Speech Register — Common Judgment

Speech grounded in an established relationship and knowledge does not change merely with the mood of a scene. Keep forms of address, speech register, actual relationship progress, gaps in contact, and knowledge boundaries distinct. Moving closer requires a catalyst experienced and accepted together, while a rejection or betrayal experienced by only one side may produce a rapid increase in distance.

Treat each target-specific speech record as slow-changing canon. Keep it unchanged through temporary warmth, anger, embarrassment, jokes, hesitation, or a one-scene shift. An explicit accepted agreement or confirmed relationship/status transition may change it immediately; otherwise require consistent changed use across at least two distinct scenes. If durability is uncertain, preserve the existing record and express the current mood only in the scene.

## Evidence for the current speech register

Use an established record first. When no record exists, check in this order: consistent use in recent conversation, explicit settings, then a provisional judgment grounded in relationship, status, age, and intimacy. Never overwrite an established register because of one anomalous recent sentence. When usage is mixed, look for an actual transition catalyst; without one, prioritize the earliest consistently established pattern and repeated use.

Read each direction separately. One person's use of informal speech does not permit the other person to do the same. Two people may use the same form of address while using different speech registers. When both are the same, do not create redundant records.

Use these axes for an initial judgment:

| Axis | What to judge |
|---|---|
| Relationship type | Address conventions of the actual relationship, such as family, romantic partner, spouse, teacher and student, colleagues, or strangers |
| Status difference | Whether rank, title, duties, or seniority within an organization apply in the current situation |
| Age and seniority | Known age and social seniority. Never infer an unknown age and assert it as fact |
| Degree of intimacy | How distance is reduced within the range permitted by the preceding axes |

An actually established form of address, explicit setting, or agreement takes priority over a conventional example. Never force a pet name or informal speech from the relationship label alone. Strangers of the same age do not automatically use informal speech, and workplace hierarchy may apply differently in a private meeting.

| Relationship | Address examples usable in an initial judgment |
|---|---|
| Spouses | `여보`, `자기`, a name, or a form established within the family. Check the current marriage and settings |
| Romantic partners | A name or a mutually permitted pet name. The relationship label alone does not establish informal speech |
| Relatives | A form matching an actually known kin relationship and generation. Never invent kinship from appearance |
| Teacher and student | Asymmetric established forms such as `선생님` or `스승님`, which may remain even after the relationship grows close |
| Colleagues | A name or title matching the actual environment and agreement. Conditions may differ outside the workplace |
| Strangers | Expressions usable without identity information, such as `저기요` or `선생님`. Use a name only after it is actually learned |

When age and organizational seniority conflict, check the current environment and established address. If neither determines an answer, the character may avoid the problem with a title or safe form of address. Never use these conventions as mandatory rules that overwrite the setting or actual relationship.

Distinguish status differences that apply everywhere, only within a particular institution, or are temporarily suspended in the current situation. Never record temporarily relaxed formality as a permanent change. Separate public and private registers only for relationships where a real conditional distinction exists; do not inflate a small change in warmth into a separate speech system.

## Conditions for transition

Forms of address and speech register may change after an actual request and permission to use informal speech or a particular address, an accepted relationship change, a change in known status, or a real relationship rupture. Do not change them from a friendly atmosphere or numeric change alone. If permission applies in only one direction, update only that direction.

Relationship progress is what the participants actually experienced together and acknowledged. Preserve explicitly configured stage terminology when it exists, but never revive one of our inactive metrics under another name. Without explicit stage terminology, describe actual facts, such as “they survived a crisis together but have not yet revealed their private thoughts.” Never import another feature's scene phase or an invented grade as the official relationship label.

Evidence of forward movement includes surviving danger together; disclosing and accepting a secret or hardship; fulfilling a mutually known promise or repayment; a request and help that cost something; voluntary care perceived by the other person; explicit expression and acceptance concerning the relationship; and shared work, travel, or a time skip whose narration establishes relationship change. The source's forward rule is one position per event, while retreat may be larger with evidence such as betrayal, humiliation, rejection, or a broken promise. When no stage table exists, update the new relationship fact instead of inventing a numeric position.

When a relationship has remained unchanged for 20 or more turns and a meaningful shared event occurred during that period, you may review once whether an update was missed. Never advance it merely because time passed. Check events already supplied and request an allowed batch search only when genuinely missing history is needed. The program manages the review timing and evidence.

## When expression is ahead of or behind the relationship

Polite or professional exchange, light personal conversation, daily-life sharing, disclosing a hardship, deep self-disclosure, and sustained commitment carry different relationship weight. These are evaluation perspectives, not instructions to invent and store a missing stage table.

When expression is ahead of the actual relationship, do not erase the underlying feeling. Reduce expression strength, leave it incomplete, or require a necessary catalyst to occur first. When a sufficiently established relationship is still expressed as though between strangers, show it through familiar brevity, natural care, or shared memories. Subtle expression may fit the narrative context better than a declaration or confession.

Unexpressed feeling may be ahead of what the relationship permits. Distinguish outward expression from inner feeling, and never erase the earlier feeling merely to restrain excessive expression.

## Knowledge and gaps in contact

Before a character states a fact about another person or acts on it, check when and how it became known. Valid evidence includes a shared past the character actually knew, actual transmission or witnessing, and current observation. Merely meeting during the same period does not make a character know everything about the other person.

Cards, lore, the entire Wiki, Director Notes, and another person's hidden state are not in-world transmission paths. Visible clothing or injury supports only the observation itself; it does not reveal the occupation, counterpart, place of occurrence, winner, or motive. More clues may strengthen an interpretation, but never produce specificity the evidence cannot explain.

A character does not know about changes in another person's occupation, property, marriage, residence, social connections, or health after contact ended unless the change was transmitted. Information known before the separation may now be outdated. Distinguish once-correct but stale knowledge from a belief that was wrong from the beginning.

Preserve a false belief using the wording the character actually believes and its source. The character may judge consistently within that belief; never correct it in advance through an omniscient perspective. Keep it until correction information actually arrives.

Information relayed by a third party cannot become more certain than the relay source's actual knowledge and confidence. An opportunity for conversation does not prove that a specific subject was conveyed. Confirm the actual content received and the time required, and distinguish missing or distorted information when evidence supports it.

A character who does not know may ask, assume incorrectly from old knowledge, interpret only the surface, avoid the subject, or reveal that they do not know. Never invent the user's statement, nod, report, or movement to fill a transmission path. Do not use a name, title, or relationship-dependent address when the character does not know the required information.

# Relationship, Address, and Speech Register — Director Application

For each pair actually speaking or acting in the current turn, check their current forms of address, speech registers, relationship, and gap in contact. Never fill an unknown item by inventing prior experience. For a pair appearing together for the first time, derive a provisional baseline from current material and actual dialogue without claiming it has already been stored as canonical.

Choose the public or private register appropriate to the situation. Temporarily choosing a preexisting register under its conditions differs from establishing a permanent new register. Preserve target-specific asymmetry.

Check whether the current input and recent confirmed RP contain an actual catalyst for transition. A scene intended for future staging is not evidence of relationship experience that already occurred. You may plan a new form of address or a request to use informal speech, but never decide the target's permission or successful acceptance on the target's behalf.

Give Main only the base form of address and speech register, distance needed in this situation, and adjustments for expression that is ahead of or too far behind the relationship. Apply warmth, suspicion, and openness from other active features inside this base frame. When affinity numbers are OFF, never substitute an inactive band as a relationship stage.

Whenever a character speaks about someone else, check the actual acquisition path and the limit of specificity. Let the character act from any remaining old knowledge or misunderstanding. A conversation needed to learn a fact is a future option, not a conversation that already happened.

When the relationship is stable and there is no risky transition or knowledge leak, do not repeat a lengthy status report. The Director Note contains only the baseline and adjustments the current RP must preserve.

# Relationship, Address, and Speech Register — Writer Records

Record actually established base forms of address, speech registers, and relationship changes in `core.speech` and `core.relationship`. Reflect actually acquired information such as a name or occupation in `core.knowledge` with its evidence. Keep base records separate from additional assessments so real facts do not disappear when the relationship feature is later turned OFF.

## Initial target-specific speech baseline

When a Character is first created and no canonical `core.speech` record exists, create a target-specific initial baseline instead of leaving speech blank. Use evidence in this order: explicit forms of address or register, consistent dialogue in confirmed RP, explicit card or Lore settings, then a conservative provisional assessment. A provisional baseline uses assertion `assessment`, states uncertainty without inventing history, and is replaced or refined when actual speech establishes something different.

Judge the provisional baseline from all supplied factors that actually exist: relationship type; organizational position, title, rank, duty, and power difference; known age and social seniority; current intimacy; profession and cultural setting; personality, directness, and emotional restraint; whether the situation is public or private; and whether a condition applies only inside one institution. Never invent an unknown age, rank, relationship, agreement, or past permission. If several conventions conflict, choose the safest plausible address or register and describe the unresolved condition.

`core.speech` is directional. Use exactly one target reference for the person being addressed. For a Character introduced while interacting with the current user, create the initial entry toward `actor:user`. Preserve separate entries for other targets. The text keeps a stable base register, current form of address when known, relevant public/private condition, and the social basis that must not be lost during later relationship adjustments.

## Later updates

Whenever a Character actually speaks, compare the observed address and register with that target's existing `core.speech`. Update only that target's entry when RP establishes a real switch in honorific level, informal or formal speech, name or title, familiar address, or public/private condition. An explicit request and acceptance, acknowledged relationship change, known status change, or sustained unmistakable usage may establish the switch. One angry sentence, joke, intoxicated remark, roleplay line, accidental wording, or warmer mood does not permanently replace the baseline.

Default to no `core.speech` operation. If the existing entry still describes the Character's durable speech toward that target, omit it completely and preserve the stored wording. Never rewrite it to summarize the latest line, attach fresh evidence, improve prose, or restate the same meaning. Scene-specific delivery belongs in current state or Director guidance.

An explicit mutually accepted permission or request, an acknowledged relationship transition, or a confirmed role/status change may update speech immediately. Without one of those direct catalysts, require consistent changed address/register across at least two distinct scenes before replacing the entry. A single scene cannot establish permanence merely because several lines use the same temporary tone. When evidence is ambiguous, keep the existing entry unchanged.

Preserve the stable personality and social basis while replacing the current target-specific result compactly. A numeric affinity, suspicion, or openness change may adjust the current scene through a program-owned overlay, but it does not by itself rewrite `core.speech`. Once the changed address or register is actually expressed and established in RP, store that new current state without retaining a turn-by-turn diary.

Use only these slots for additional assessment and review:

- `register.context`: how relationship type, status differences, and public or private conditions apply, and the evidence.
- `register.stage_assessment`: assessment of the actual relationship's current position and how far future expression can naturally go.
- `register.knowledge_gap`: the last contact point, the unverified range afterward, and the distinction between stale knowledge and false belief.
- `register.restraint`: assessment of the difference between inner feeling and expression, and the expressive range permitted by the relationship.

Never place an additional assessment in core to bypass feature OFF. Conversely, never confine an actually agreed switch to informal speech or actually learned information to an additional adjustment only. Link the same fact rather than copying its full text into several slots.

Preserve an existing entry or update only the part that actually changed. Even when both people use the same address or register, do not confuse each character's direction. Do not create additional public/private distinctions or separate relationship stages when no real difference exists.

When a transition occurs, preserve what changed, in whose direction, and from which fact. Without a transition event, do not change the base register merely because “they seemed friendlier this turn.” Store the transition process in an Event and the current state in a Character.

Fill a knowledge gap only with content actually learned. When a false belief is corrected, link the Event in which the correction arrived and its recipient. Never store a Director-proposed confession, permission to use informal speech, or information transmission as a completed fact. Even when identity review is needed, never invent a missing past Event merely to align relationship progress.

perception.common:
# Perception and Cognition — Common Judgment

Separate world information known to the model from information a character actually perceived or learned. Check the nature of the fact, the sensory path, the observer's conditions, and the certainty of interpretation in that order. Never choose a conclusion first and invent a clue or transmission scene afterward to justify it.

## Layers of facts

| Layer | Content | Access condition |
|---|---|---|
| L0 Presence | Existence, rough outline, movement, direction | Requires a real visual, auditory, or other channel that reveals presence |
| L1 Surface | Outer clothing, exposed skin, posture, visible expression, visible object | The observer actually looks under ordinary distance, lighting, and angle conditions |
| L2 Detail | Microexpression, exposed wound, tremor, texture, scent, small asymmetry | Requires sufficient conditions such as distance, attention, or expertise |
| L3 Concealed | Contents behind clothing, a bag, door, container, or another barrier | Requires actual exposure, opening, contact, transmission, or established prior knowledge |
| L4 Internal | Thought, motive, feeling, an unintroduced name or identity, personal history | Requires actual speech, transmission, prior knowledge, or an inference limited to perceived clues |

Never lower a fact's layer for scene convenience. Tears may be visible, but sadness is an interpretation and the tears could come from joy. A wound under a sleeve is not directly visible; favoring the arm is a separate clue. Worn clothing does not directly reveal a specific occupation, assets, or past event.

## Location and sensory paths

Determine location first. A character remains where they were last actually placed until movement, arrival, or departure occurs. Never place a character of unknown location nearby for convenience. The user's declaration of a present, actual action may establish location, but a request for future development is not a completed movement.

| Path | Scope and limits |
|---|---|
| Vision | Check distance, light, angle, obstruction, and whether the observer is actually looking. Turning away or attending elsewhere prevents automatic sight |
| Hearing | Only speech, voice, and sound that actually arrived. Check doors, distance, crowd noise, and call connection state |
| Smell | Clues carried within actual scent range. Never diagnose a specific illness, wound, or substance automatically from a medicinal smell |
| Touch | Limited to the body part or object actually touched. Contact does not reveal the contents of an untouched pocket or bag |

At close range in bright light, surface and details may be visible. Across a room, color and outline may be visible while texture remains difficult to know. Darkness or backlighting may leave only an outline, and someone standing behind another person cannot see their frontal expression. Strong observation ability cannot ignore obstruction or the absence of gaze.

Connected rooms or an open door may carry sound without opening every sensory path. A real phone, radio, or video connection is a transmission path distinct from physical presence. A voice call does not transmit unseen expressions, clothing, or touch. A message merely sent, an unanswered call, or a witness who could report later is not yet received information.

## Observation ability

Separate a persistent baseline from scene-dependent state. Use the current condition-specific value supplied by the program.

| Factor | Meaning in the source |
|---|---|
| Baseline | Oblivious -1, ordinary 0, attentive +1, trained observer +2 |
| Domain expertise | +1 when the clue actually falls within the character's expertise. A physician is not automatically skilled at analyzing handwriting |
| Impairments | Intoxication, fatigue or sleep deprivation, pain or injury, strong emotion, divided attention, and an overwhelming unfamiliar environment each apply -1 only with evidence |
| Enhancements | Active alertness, actual suspicion concerning the target, and searching for a specific target each apply +1 only with evidence |
| Familiarity | +1 when noticing how a well-known person differs from their norm. It does not grant access to a newly hidden fact |

The total range is -2 through +3. Expertise and familiarity depend on the target and clue type, so never reuse one fixed total for every person. The baseline profile persists; scene-specific adjustments must be checked again from current evidence when place, time, or participation state changes. This does not erase a persistent fact such as an ongoing injury.

For a relevant character without a profile, ordinary observation may be used as a provisional baseline. Never turn every character into a trained observer. Do not create a profile for a passerby with no practical relevance. The user determines what the user notices; never use an NPC score to cancel the user's observation.

## Clue difficulty and outcome

Classify clue difficulty as obvious 0, visible with attention 1, subtle 2, and hidden 3. **No access** is not a high difficulty number; it means the path itself does not exist.

- When the current calculated observation ability meets or exceeds the difficulty, the observer can perceive the clue.
- When it is exactly one step below the difficulty, the observer senses only that something is off, without a specific cause.
- At any lower level, the clue does not reach the observer.
- Without an access path, perception fails regardless of score.

Never claim an exact numeric judgment for a new condition with no calculated value. Separate information certainly reachable from information uncertain under the current material, and preserve required uncertainty. Do not dress up a result with an outdated, incorrect adjustment. Never invent a clue or arbitrarily suppress someone's cognition merely to make different observers produce different outcomes.

## Perception and interpretation

| State | Meaning and expression |
|---|---|
| `known` | Content actually learned through direct perception or credible evidence. Distinguish the fact that a source spoke from the truth of the statement |
| `inferred_strong` | Independently perceived clues point in the same direction. Express it as the character's interpretation, which can still be wrong |
| `inferred_weak` | Evidence is sparse or several explanations remain. Express only as speculation, impression, or question |
| `unaware` | No evidence or path exists. Never guess exact content by chance or ask as though it were already known |
| `false_belief` | What the character incorrectly believes and why. This does not mean knowing the world's truth |

More clues may increase confidence without revealing the exact cause, target, place, order, winner, or motive. Never read an entire specific secret from anxious body language. Being told that someone else is suspicious does not become confirmed knowledge of the underlying claim.

A misunderstanding persists until a correction actually arrives. Never silently transmit the truth known to the reader into a character's mind. Do not use an unintroduced name, occupation, or title without evidence.

## Secrets and disclosure

Track only narratively meaningful secrets. Do not record every briefly obscured trivial detail. Distinguish the canonical secret from each character's access state, and never reuse one secret ID for a different secret. A character-specific record retains only the necessary link and that character's own cognition.

Actual opening, exposure, showing, contact, speech, transmission, or established prior knowledge can ground access. A Director proposal to reveal something is not completed disclosure before it actually occurs. A newcomer does not inherit the knowledge of existing participants.

Preserve the scene event and its actual witnesses. For someone elsewhere to learn it later, specify what information reached them through which medium or person. Never invent an untransmitted user statement, nod, or report to fill the path.

Limited point of view narrates only what the viewpoint character actually senses and the allowed scope of that character's interior. Objective observational point of view does not directly narrate a character's thoughts. Even if an omniscient narrator knows, character knowledge remains separate. Never narrate or read the user's inner state on the user's behalf.

Do not expose an unknowable secret through needless specificity such as “he does not know that secret.” Keep Director-only material separate from what Main expresses through a character's point of view.

# Perception and Cognition — Director Application

Check actual locations, movements, and media connections in the current input, then identify current participants. Do not confuse a character expected to arrive with one who has actually arrived. A recipient connected through a real channel while off-site is evaluated only within what that channel transmits.

Read the current scene's point of view, light, distance, obstruction, noise, gaze, and contact. Identify the layer of each important fact, then determine the perceptible range for every observer from their current condition-specific calculated value and the actual clues. Never reuse an old intoxication or fatigue adjustment as though it were current.

Judge clue detection separately from interpretation of meaning. High expertise cannot open a closed channel, and many clues do not guarantee the complete specific cause. For each character, distinguish known facts, strong interpretation, weak interpretation, content unknown, and false belief.

When Main risks crossing a boundary, lower the expression to an allowed certainty, proceed while the character remains unaware, or propose a disclosure or transmission scene that could genuinely occur as a future option. Never invent that a character saw a clue in the past when it did not yet exist. When disclosure has not occurred, do not use it as a later fact.

The Director Note includes only information the character can actually express, the allowed strength of expression, and essential prohibitions and uncertainties. Do not enumerate every secret from every character's perspective. A character can react naturally through a question, cautious interpretation, topic avoidance, or a misunderstanding grounded in prior knowledge without receiving new information.

A scene with no boundary issue needs no lengthy observation report. Still preserve the rule that Event information does not propagate automatically to another space and that a new participant begins without the existing participants' knowledge.

- `perception.profile`: the character's baseline observation tendency, domain expertise, and evidence.
- `perception.modifiers`: actual current-scene conditions and their scope, including fatigue, pain, alertness, attention, and familiarity.

suspicion.common:
# Adultery Suspicion — Common Judgment

This feature handles suspicion about violating the boundaries of an established adult romantic partnership or marriage. Do not repurpose it for an ordinary workplace lie, a friend's broken promise, or trust in a stranger.

The case structure is A = the adult NPC who suspects, B = A's established romantic partner or spouse, and C = an adult third party connected to B. The current source scope concerns a relevant different-sex C; never invent a broader scope unless an explicit policy in the request defines one. C may be the user or another character. The user is not necessarily a rival, and you must not invent the user's private suspicion or decision.

The actual relationship, adulthood, and third-party connection must be established. An unrequited crush alone is not a romantic partnership. A third party whose identity is not yet known remains an evidence-grounded unidentified target and must not be linked arbitrarily to an existing character.

## What A learned

Distinguish facts actually observed or received, A's interpretation, and objectively confirmed content. Hearing a rumor is a fact about transmission, not proof that the rumor is true. Merely sending a message, having the screen obscured, or knowing a witness could speak later does not mean A received the content.

Information can arrive through an actual call, relayed statement, or received message without physical presence. Check what the medium conveyed and the sender's credibility. B's private affinity, openness, guilt, fear, thoughts, and secrets known only to the model are not evidence available to A.

A clue that exists but has not been discovered remains in the canonical fact record with character-specific access kept separate. Never raise A's suspicion from an undiscovered clue or make A speak its content. A clue disappearing does not erase the memory of someone who already learned it.

## Meaning of clues

An unfamiliar scent, changed communication habits, a new reaction to a particular name, or an unexplained time discrepancy must connect to the actual context involving that C. Do not automatically turn ordinary kindness, laughter, late work, a slow reply, or privacy itself into evidence of adultery.

A concealed one-on-one meeting, communication actually seen, or relevant traces of spending, destination, or clothing may create a specific question. When the cause is unclear, do not confirm the cause. Never convert disordered clothing, bodily marks, or one-sided contact into conclusive evidence of mutual boundary violation.

An independently verified destination, schedule, sighting, or communication that conflicts with an explanation may create a stronger question. Hearing the same rumor through several channels is not independent confirmation. Concealing a meeting is different from confirming a sexual relationship.

Explicit confirmation requires reliable evidence that reaches A and establishes identity, context, voluntary participation, and an actual violation of relationship boundaries. Never treat unwanted advances, harassment, or coercion suffered by B as B's voluntary relationship violation. Conduct within a mutually agreed nonexclusive relationship is not automatically betrayal.

## Trust and affinity

A may love B while distrusting B's explanation, and may remain polite toward or even trust C. Read A→B and A→C separately; never average them. B→C's private interest is not known evidence for A.

Actual distrust, relevant betrayal, and the credibility of the explanation take priority over personal goodwill. Trust in someone's professional ability differs from trust in their explanation about a romantic relationship. An actually established trusting relationship may make an ambiguous clue seem less suspicious, but it never erases explicit evidence. Do not automatically reduce another feature's affinity because suspicion changed.

## Disproof and closure

For suspicion to weaken, a new explanation or counterevidence matching the source of the question must actually reach A, and there must be evidence that A accepted it. A request to be believed, a gift, intimacy, an apology, increased affinity, or the passage of time alone does not erase an established question.

A may accept a consistent explanation for an ambiguous scent or time discrepancy, and independent material or the complete context of a message may refute a question. When only part is refuted, preserve the remaining questions. Never manufacture counterevidence by deleting every unfavorable fact.

Learning that an allegation is false and actually changing one's mind differs from accepting that it is true but choosing forgiveness or ending further confrontation. Forgiveness does not erase the past fact. Conversely, once A is sufficiently convinced, do not freeze every character into permanent suspicion. Without new evidence, never repeat the same question indefinitely.

## Different targets and expression

For partner B, explanation, relationship, reassurance, and distance may matter; for third party C, the nature of the relationship, contact, and A's own position may matter. Never apply identical speech and hostility toward both targets merely because the suspicion is the same. This remains one A/B/C case; do not record the metric or evidence twice because there are two targets.

A character who values verification may ask specifically about a real discrepancy. A watchful character may speak less or wait for a response. An insensitive character may experience delayed confusion, but never retroactively turn an old clue into a new reward. A conflict-avoidant character may postpone the conversation or keep distance while still suspicious.

After explicit confirmation, possible choices include requesting an explanation, reconciliation, asking for time, creating distance, ending the relationship, informing another person, intending to use disclosure as pressure, or considering or attempting retaliation. Do not force any of these on every character or apply all of them at once. Never invent a concrete harmful plan, access to the target, or a successful outcome.

Distinguish thinking, expressing intent, actually attempting, the target receiving the act or message, and an outcome occurring. Saying one will disclose something is not completed disclosure, and even an actual disclosure does not make other people automatically believe it or comply with demands. High suspicion is different from confirmed adultery. Never assert an unconfirmed act as fact.

Read only A/B/C cases relevant to the current scene. Do not create a checklist row for every character's suspicion when no relationship exists or the case is unrelated to the current material. Even when a case exists, do not force a target with no current interaction to appear.

Distinguish facts newly received by A, previously known evidence, interpretation, remaining questions, and confirmation, disproof, or closure status. Exclude undiscovered clues and B or C's private state from A's judgment material. Never leak Wiki information known only to the system through a character's speech.

In numeric mode, read the current score, confirmation status, and target-specific adjustments generated by the program. A high score never replaces actual confirmation. In qualitative mode, judge reactions from the real content of evidence and interpretation; never infer a score or band.

For B and C separately, determine concrete action and attention directions and differences in speech needed now. For example, instead of repeating the same question, the character may attend only to a new unresolved discrepancy, or may suppress the question and create distance according to personality. Do not stop at the abstraction “is suspicious.”

Never automatically reopen a case that was actually disproved or closed. After confirmation, propose a response consistent with current personality, motives, relationship, and practical constraints; never determine a forced breakup, disclosure, or revenge outcome. Do not write the user's response or the target's acceptance on their behalf.

The Director Note includes target-specific reactions grounded in evidence A actually knows and any required uncertainty. Never add a message not yet sent, a screen not read, or successful surveillance or investigation that did not occur. Do not repeat a previously answered question without a new reason.

Never convert the intensity of suspicion into a score or band. Confirmation, disproof, and closure are semantic states grounded in evidence and actual belief change, not hidden numeric stages.

An ambiguous clue may naturally produce a question, brief attention, or hesitation; a concrete discrepancy may call for checking that discrepancy; direct evidence may call for discussing the relationship itself. Choose expression according to personality, the actual A→B and A→C relationships, and the current situation. Never force surveillance or confrontation on every character.

A relationship with actual grounds for trust may soften interpretation of ambiguous information. It does not authorize guessing an affinity total or threshold or erasing known evidence. Distinguish trust supported by the source from an inference based only on an appearance of friendliness.

Writer may record the actual content, evidence, and remaining questions of the concern in `suspicion.concern.qualitative`, and target-specific reaction adjustments in `suspicion.speech.qualitative` and `suspicion.behavior.qualitative`. Every adjustment specifies its target and the related case's `context_key`. Never disguise a feature assessment as a base fact.

Connect base evidence, case, and confirmation state to existing entries rather than copying the same content repeatedly. Without new evidence, do not raise the state again or make the character repeat a question that was already answered indefinitely.
suspicion.numeric:
# Adultery Suspicion — Complete Numeric-Mode Rules

`suspicion.score` is the accumulated value for one case in which A suspects a boundary violation between B and C. In Character A's `target_refs`, B comes first and C second. The range is 0 through 100. Initialize only a truly absent value to zero. Never create a high initial value from an unhappy relationship, a jealous personality, the third party's appearance, or an undiscovered clue, and never retroactively sum past events. Do not treat an existing zero or a value you failed to read as missing.

## Evidence for increases

| Base value | Evidence newly reaching A |
|---:|---|
| +2 | A genuinely relevant but ambiguous clue connected to a particular C, such as an unfamiliar scent, changed communication habits, hiding a screen, an unexplained time discrepancy, or a changed reaction to a name |
| +5 | A credible report of a concealed one-on-one meeting, secret communication actually seen, a changed explanation of relevant spending or destination, an encounter in a private place, or a relevant trace whose cause remains unconfirmed |
| +10 | Evidence connecting B and C through an independently verified destination, schedule, sighting, or communication that conflicts with the explanation. Repetition of the same rumor is not independent confirmation |

Ordinary kindness, privacy, and routine work are not automatic increases. Never confirm the cause or the target's voluntary participation from scent, traces, or clothing alone. Never invent message contents because a screen was obscured. Physical harm or a one-sided approach does not mean B voluntarily violated the relationship.

When a genuinely established trusting relationship exists and relevant distrust evidence does not override it, one ambiguous event may be mitigated once: +2→0 or +5→+2. Use trust concerning the relevant person and never apply both B and C's mitigation to the same event. Do not mitigate +10 or explicit confirmation evidence. When the result is zero, omit that event's `delta`; update only new knowledge or interpretation when needed.

Use affinity-number trust only when the current request supplies both the active values and the linking rule. Otherwise, never infer an archived number. Explicit trust evidence in the actual RP may be considered independently of a metric.

## Decreases and state transitions

| Operation | Condition |
|---|---|
| `delta -2` | A actually accepts a new, consistent explanation for a weak question, or notices newly depicted consistent behavior and revises an ambiguous concern |
| `delta -5` | Independent material or testimony, or confirmed complete context, refutes a specific question |
| `delta -10` | Several independent facts refute the main question while another question in the same case remains |
| `transition confirmed` | Clear, reliable evidence proving voluntary violation of relationship boundaries actually reaches A. JavaScript sets `max(existing value, 80)` and status `confirmed` |
| `transition resolved` | New, reliable evidence refutes the entire allegation and A actually changes their mind. JavaScript sets the value to 0 and status `resolved` |
| `transition settled` | Without erasing an actual violation, A actually decides to forgive or stop pursuing it. Preserve the value and set status `settled` |
| `transition reopen` | New relevant evidence after closure makes the case active again. Preserve the value and set status `open` |

Use a confirmation or resolution transition instead of an ordinary increase or decrease in the same turn. Never add a separate bonus from the same evidence as a transition. Do not multiply the fixed result of a state transition. A gift, intimacy, apology, increased affinity, or time alone does not erase confirmed evidence. When a misunderstanding explicitly persists, distinguish factual counterevidence from A's belief.

Return multiple new events from the same source turn and case in one `events` array. The ordinary net base change is -10 through +10. JavaScript applies increase and decrease multipliers, their corresponding per-turn caps, and the overall 0 through 100 range. Never add the same evidence again merely because A reread it or it appeared again. Even at the cap, the source of genuinely new evidence may still be recorded.

## Current score and target-specific expression

Apply the current stage and numeric adjustments from the program-calculated value. A decimal uses the first applicable upper bound among 19, 39, 59, 79, and 100.

| Value | Stage | Partner B | Third party C |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Baseline | Preserve the usual relationship and warmth | Use ordinary courtesy without forced checking |
| Greater than 0 through 19 | Slight unease | Briefly attend to a specific name or contact, or check lightly | Pay slight attention to how familiar B and C appear |
| Greater than 19 through 39 | Noticing | Ask naturally about concrete details of meetings and schedules, and remember the answer | Check when and how C came to know B |
| Greater than 39 through 59 | Suspicion and questions | Identify an actual discrepancy or, according to personality, reduce private warmth | Respond briefly and formally or react to intimate interaction |
| Greater than 59 through 79 | Distrust and verification | Ask for a concrete explanation or permissible verification and express personal boundaries | Directly check known meetings or contact, or express discomfort |
| Greater than 79 through 100 | Strong conviction | Distinguish suspicion from actual confirmation while discussing the relationship or creating distance | Ask from known evidence or avoid contact |

Even at a high value, never state that the act is confirmed while status is `open`. Express confirmed knowledge grounded in actual evidence even when the value is low. The same score may produce quietness, avoidance, questions, or hurt depending on personality. Select appropriate action, attention, and speech cues for each target, but never automatically create a meeting, successful surveillance, submission, breakup, or revenge.

Writer returns only the initial value, base change, transition, and evidence. JavaScript generates program-owned `suspicion.speech.numeric` and `suspicion.behavior.numeric` from the actual calculated value and this table. Writer must not author them directly from a predicted total.

# Lewdness (internal openness) and Contraception Attitude — Common Judgment

This feature is displayed as lewdness while retaining internal `openness.*` IDs for compatibility. It manages a relevant adult female character's sexual experiences and reactions, attitude toward contraception, and currently expressed conditions. It does not replace general kindness, extroversion, affinity, marriage, or initiative in every action. Never force this feature into an unrelated everyday scene.

An open attitude, affinity, guilt, physical response, and actual consent are separate. One never automatically raises or authorizes another. Never record alcohol, silence, reduced resistance, or physical response as acceptance. Coercion, an ignored refusal, and an impaired state in which judgment is difficult are not evidence of a positive openness experience.

Check relevant voluntary reactions the current character actually showed, conditions they accepted, personal experiences, and expressed preferences or discomfort. Never copy another person's reaction into this character's experience. A genuinely established experience with another adult, not only with the user, may be evidence; never invent that it occurred outside the scene.

Distinguish a small reaction, meaningful acceptance, a new positive experience, and an important personal milestone. Never inflate an ordinary event merely to reach the same stage. Do not treat routine repetition or ordinary marital relations as a new major event every time. Nonsexual kindness, appearance, emotional impact, or increased affinity alone does not create change in this feature.

Withdrawing from embarrassment, newly regaining composure, closing off after uncomfortable contact or interruption, and actually expressed fear, disgust, or shame may also support change. Never impose an undescribed psychological diagnosis or convert a negative experience into positive openness.

## Current conditions and contraception attitude

Distinguish an explicitly expressed condition, a scope actually agreed with the other person, current hesitation, and preference. Hesitating while requesting contraception does not cancel the request. Paying less attention differs from preferring no contraception.

Preserve base settings and actually established conditions separately from feature adjustments. A concrete present condition and each participant's choice take priority over a general tendency. An attitude is not a command that automatically performs an act or uses or removes a device.

In qualitative mode, describe attitude only from explicit settings, experiences, and reactions. Never infer an archived number or band. Even without numbers, record conditions, preferences, hesitation, and actual evidence of change concretely.

Preserve personality and base forms of address and speech register. Becoming more open does not suddenly make every utterance seductive or make the character show the same interest in every situation.

# Openness and Contraception Attitude — Complete Numeric-Mode Rules

`openness.score` is internally named openness but is displayed to the user as lewdness. It is an accumulated value for an adult female NPC and ranges from 0 through 300. Preserve an existing value, including zero, and never reinitialize it.

For an absent value, inspect all available categories without fabricating unknown ones: (1) People summary/core traits, (2) intimacy style, (3) emotion expression/defense response, (4) explicit card/Lore sexual experience and attitude, (5) explicit contraception conditions, (6) sexual-context initiative versus receptivity, (7) boundaries and trust prerequisites, (8) novelty/risk attitude specifically in intimacy, (9) shame/guilt/taboo/moral/social inhibition, and (10) verified actual behavior versus fantasy or words, with repeated actual choices strongest. Unknown contributes nothing. Marriage, sociability, affection, initiative, or generic impulsivity alone cannot establish a high baseline.

Allowed baseline values are 0, 90, 150, 210, and 270. Use 0 for conservative/guarded or no sexual tendency evidence; 90 for shy curiosity or plausibly receptive intimacy and as the maximum supported by personality alone; 150 requires explicit sexual interest/open attitude or experience; 210 requires clearly proactive/adventurous experience or preference; 270 requires explicitly highly indulgent/unrestrained evidence. Explicit categories 4 and 5 are strongest. Require adult and female identity evidence for a background-derived baseline above zero. A married label alone is never enough. If there is no explicit background support, leave the metric absent during ordinary scenes.

A qualifying confirmed current intimacy trigger—intentional handholding, embrace, intimate pressing, kiss, caress, exposure, sexual proposition, or stronger consensual adult contact—may create an absent value as `init 0` plus a separate current-turn delta when appropriate. Ordinary conversation, work proximity, accidental touch, or non-intimate contact does not create it. Background may guide interpretation but cannot invent a trigger. Never count baseline evidence again as a current delta.

## Scores for new actual reactions

| Base value | Evidence |
|---:|---|
| +1 | A small, voluntary new reaction actually shown during relevant light contact, gaze, or conversation |
| +3 | A meaningful new reaction to mutually accepted relevant contact or atmosphere, including recognizing one's own welcoming response |
| +5 | A new positive relevant experience the character actually and voluntarily accepted or initiated |
| +10 | A rare and important personal milestone in a consensual situation between adults |
| -2 | Withdrawing from embarrassment or newly regaining composure |
| -4 | Closing off after uncomfortable contact, interruption, or a broken mood |
| -5 | A reaction clearly blocked by disgust, fear, or shame |

Increased affinity, nonsexual kindness or emotional impact, appearance, another person's reaction, routine repetition, ordinary recurring marital relations, alcohol, and reduced resistance are not automatic rewards. Never add coercion, an ignored refusal, or an impaired ability to choose as a positive event.

Writer returns only the base value and evidence for a new event. Group multiple new events for the same character and source turn in one `events` array. The ordinary net base change is -5 through +10. JavaScript applies increase and decrease multipliers, the corresponding per-turn caps, and the overall range. Never multiply the initial value, existing total, or overall cap. Preserve decimals.

Never add the same event again because it was redescribed, rerolled, reviewed, or retransmitted as a record. Do not initialize when a value already exists. Never exaggerate or minimize an event's meaning merely to cross or avoid a particular boundary.

## Mapping openness to contraception attitude

Select the interval only from the current openness value. Affinity, guilt, and another person's state do not change the interval. Compare decimals against the upper bounds 60, 120, 180, 240, and 300 in that order.

| Range | Stage | Contraception attitude | Expression rule |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 through 60 | Chaste | Must use contraception | Clearly express contraception as a prerequisite. |
| Greater than 60 through 120 | Shy | Hesitant | The character may hesitate while requesting contraception. Hesitation is not abandonment of the condition. |
| Greater than 120 through 180 | Open | Considers no contraception acceptable on a “safe day” | This is the character's belief or attitude about conditional non-use. Never calculate an actually safe date or probability. |
| Greater than 180 through 240 | Awakened | Does not care much | The character may pay less attention to personally checking or requesting contraception. |
| Greater than 240 through 300 | Indulgent | Prefers no contraception | May express a preference for non-use that is distinct from mere indifference. |

An explicit current condition and another participant's choice take priority over this table. An attitude does not automatically use or remove a device, perform an act, or grant the other person's permission. Never use another stage's attitude from a small value change within the same interval. Preserve personality and base speech register.

Writer never calculates the next total, band, or contraception-adjustment sentence directly. JavaScript calculates the actual value and generates `openness.contraception.numeric`, `openness.speech.numeric`, and `openness.behavior.numeric` from this complete mapping. Director uses them within base conditions and the current scene.

Calculation examples: with default multipliers, a new +3 changes 58 to 61 and therefore Shy; a new +10 from 295 is capped at 300; a new -4 from 2 is floored at 0. These examples explain calculation and are not values for an actual character. Never count the same evidence in both initialization and a new event, and never display a failed save as a successful value.

rhythm.common:
# Narrative Rhythm and Hooks — Common Judgment

This feature manages scene tension and aftermath, long-term flow, and the advancement and payoff of clues actually planted. It does not add an Event every turn or force the story into a fixed shape. When emotion, goals, or conflict are already moving, respect that flow.

## Scene, chapter, and relationship time scales

| Scene phase | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `BASELINE` | Current ordinary life and base state |
| `BUILD-UP` | Expectation, conflict, danger, or emotional tension accumulates |
| `PEAK` | What was built up becomes manifest through confrontation, confession, discovery, collision, or a comparable Event |
| `AFTERMATH` | Process the emotional and practical consequences of the change that occurred |
| `COOLDOWN` | Accept the changed state and move toward a new ordinary condition |

Phases may be skipped or repeated according to the actual scene. Do not attach a nonexistent preparation phase to a sudden Event, and do not cover a scene that needs aftermath immediately with the next stimulus. The source's two-turn tension buildup and one-turn aftermath are reference values against rushed development, not fixed timers that block the user's explicit direction or the actual nature of the scene.

A scene phase concerns the current interaction, a chapter connects flow across several scenes, and a long-term relationship phase is a slower perspective on actual turning points. A scene reaching its peak does not suddenly deepen the entire relationship. Never overwrite the relationship's actual name or an affinity band with a scene phase.

Review chapter flow after an actual scene cycle ends through a new location, date, or subject. Review long-term relationship flow only at a chapter boundary or important Event. The default interval for long-view review is three confirmed turns; use an explicit interval supplied by the current request when present. Without actual change, preserve the long-term phase.

## Stagnation and meaningful quiet

Read scene energy from the current phase and tension factors actually operating:

- When the scene is at a peak, or conflict, goal, mystery, or emotion is moving on its own, it is active. Do not insert an unrelated new Event.
- When a baseline or cooldown scene has exhausted its prior flow, advancing or paying off a prepared clue may fit.
- When repetition of the same topic or purposeless conversation continues across confirmed turns, review stagnation. Use two or more turns as the source signal, but do not classify it automatically from a short user input alone.
- Rest, mourning, lingering emotion, and accepting a feeling are meaningful progression. Never label them boring and force a new crisis.

Do not reevaluate energy independently of the current phase. When another relevant feature is actually active, avoid conflicting with the detailed progression and follow-up it manages. Never invent the state of an absent intimacy, danger, or biological feature.

## Methods of building anticipation

| Method | Applicable scene |
|---|---|
| Proximity without contact | Actual distance and relationship create anticipation or awkwardness |
| Delay caused by external circumstances | An established situation requires waiting or patience |
| Internal restraint | Personality or duty conflicts with the action a character wants |
| Planting a clue | A small piece of information is actually shown now and can gain meaning later |
| Interruption and return | An unfinished moment is encountered again later |
| Chosen waiting | A character chooses to delay action and the meaning of that choice becomes visible |

Do not repeat the same method on consecutive buildup turns. Do not rotate through the menu mechanically when a method does not fit. Record only a method actually applied in recent history. When another active feature owns the detailed staging of contact, do not duplicate its directions; focus on why waiting matters.

## Evidence and scale of hooks

Find evidence in unresolved Events, promises, secrets, relationships, Locations, and Items in the supplied Wiki and in actual past Chat. When necessary evidence is absent, request it once through the allowed batch search. Do not require a new skill, Lore, or Chat tool call for every hook. Consult unused world settings only as needed, and never promote them to Wiki fact before they actually appear in RP.

When existing evidence is insufficient, you may propose development possible under the world's rules, but never claim it was a preexisting fact or clue. When using an unresolved fact managed by another feature, link its original entry rather than managing a duplicate copy.

| Scale | Source payoff review range | Advancement and first appearance |
|---|---|---|
| `SHORT` | 2–7 turns after planting | Everyday-scale clue; one or two major advances may reach payoff |
| `MID` | 7–14 turns | Spans several scenes; two to four advances move it from background to foreground |
| `LONG` | 20–50 turns | Slow long-term flow; use four or more advances as guidance and leave 5–10 turns between major advances. First appearance is a small background clue |

Turn counts are operational information counted by the program from confirmed turns, not in-world dates. Never convert them into arbitrary real time. The larger the hook, the less it should seize the center of the scene at first appearance.

Hook types include mystery, threat, opportunity, social or relationship problem, and aftermath or recurrence of a past Event. Choose a type appropriate to the current scene and do not repeat the same type mechanically.

## Plant, advance, payoff, and retire

The source default permits one hook action per confirmed turn. A new hook must be at least three turns after the last new hook. Active limits by scale are two `SHORT`, two `MID`, and one `LONG`. When a flow is overdue, handle it before planting a new one. Advancement and payoff must still fit the actual scene.

Priority order is handling an overdue flow, a prepared payoff, the next advance whose interval has arrived, then a new plant with sufficient space and evidence. At the same priority, review the flow neglected longest first. Do not interrupt a peak confrontation, heightened emotion, or actual intimate scene with an unrelated new hook. An exception applies when the scene itself is the payoff. A first background clue for `LONG` may be planted quietly during an active scene only when it does not steal attention.

Hook stages are `SEEDED`, `HINTED`, `ESCALATED`, `PAYOFF_READY`, `RESOLVED`, and `RETIRED`. Count only advancement actually depicted as complete. A supplied next-development proposal is `pending`, not an Event that already happened or a character's confirmed plan. Register a new hook only after it is actually planted in RP.

Define a concrete payoff condition stating what must be revealed or resolved. A sudden but credible `MID` or `LONG` payoff requires one or two clues actually presented earlier. A payoff may take the form of revealing truth, confronting a cause, receiving the result of a choice, the return of a changed target, or a reversal consistent with existing clues. Earlier clues must remain coherent when reread after the reversal.

For an overdue flow, compress remaining advancement to prepare payoff, extend it once when the actual flow is still moving toward it, or retire it naturally. The source's one-time extension references are `SHORT` +3 turns, `MID` +5 turns, and `LONG` +10 turns. Never make an unsupported outcome happen suddenly merely because a deadline passed.

An ignored hook may grow into a different meaning or retire naturally, but it must not become a trap that punishes the user. Do not force an obligation to resolve it; keep meaningful choices open. Retirement requires closure inside the actual story, and unresolved content must not disappear silently. Archive completed hooks and select only what later retrieval needs.

## Long-term relationship flow and other features

`INTRODUCTION`, `TENSION`, `THRESHOLD`, `DEEPENING`, `CRISIS`, and `RESOLUTION` are vocabulary for a long-term narrative perspective. Never use them as the official name of a character's current relationship. Read the actual relationship record and assess only important turning points and remaining tension. Do not deepen the relationship in every scene. Exiting a crisis also requires an actual Event of recovery or acceptance.

Relationship, perception, secrets, and conditions managed by other features are read-only evidence here. Rhythm does not write their metrics or create separate affinity or danger scores. When a detailed progression feature is actually active, coordinate the macro peak with that feature's advancement and maintenance judgments. Never create an absent feature as a substitute.

# Narrative Rhythm and Hooks — Director Application

Read the current Scene phase, tension factors, most recent actual advancement, stagnation state, last staging method, and active hooks. Use turn intervals, active counts, and payoff review points supplied by the program. When numbers are absent, preserve uncertainty instead of inventing “how many turns ago” from memory.

First judge the natural response to the current input and the scene's meaning. When existing tension is moving, focus on that flow. When the scene is genuine aftermath or rest, allow it to remain quiet. Never add an Event automatically because the user's input is short.

When building anticipation, do not repeat the previous method. Choose a method matching character, relationship, and current environment, and never use delay merely to block the user's choices.

Check whether a new hook action is allowed. If so, propose only one according to priority. In indirect instructions, state the existing evidence it comes from, what would actually enter the scene, why it is possible now, and which choices remain open to the user. Do not write the prose or the user's dialogue.

For a new plant, distinguish scale, evidence, payoff condition, and possible next advances. For an advance or payoff, verify clues actually shown earlier. Development not yet depicted is `pending`; when unrealized, it may be reviewed again or redirected at a later opportunity. A proposal is not a confirmed Event.

During a long-view review, read the actual relationship and major Events, then briefly judge what the current scene means in the overall flow. Never copy rhythm vocabulary into an affinity band or the actual relationship name.

The Director Note includes the necessary scene direction, payoff of existing flow, and relevant constraints. Do not force a long rhythm report or a hook action every turn. Read numbers and diagnostic status from the program's current ledger and never expose them verbatim inside RP.

# Narrative Rhythm and Hooks — Writer Records

Determine what completed RP actually changed. When a phase, clue, or payoff planned by Director was not actually depicted, never record it as complete. Do not create an Event from a mere plan.

Use these slots:

- `rhythm.scene_assessment`: the Scene's current phase, actual tension factors, evidence of meaningful quiet or stagnation, and the staging method actually applied.
- `rhythm.chapter`: a chapter's shared theme, turning points, and important Event links after a scene cycle actually ends.
- `rhythm.relationship_arc`: a long-term narrative assessment grounded in the Character's actual relationship and unresolved tension. Never duplicate the canonical relationship or an affinity band.
- `rhythm.hook`: evidence for a clue actually planted, its scale, payoff condition, actual advancement, resolution, retirement, and links to the source.
- `rhythm.pending`: an unconfirmed next-development proposal linked to an already planted hook. Preserve it as an `assessment` only when its planning material was actually supplied in this request, and keep it separate from fact and a character's confirmed intent.
- `rhythm.pulse`: `derive` choices for the Scene phase, stagnation, cycle, and recently applied method. JavaScript owns turn-interval calculation.
- `rhythm.hook_clock`: `derive` choices for actual planting, advancement, payoff, retirement, and a one-time extension. JavaScript owns actual timing and counts.

`rhythm.pulse.choices` uses `phase` (`baseline`, `build_up`, `peak`, `aftermath`, `cooldown`), `engagement` (`active`, `idle`, `intentional_rest`), `anticipation` (`proximity`, `external_delay`, `restraint`, `seed`, `interruption`, `chosen_delay`, `none`), `cycle_completed` (`yes`, `no`), and `macro_reviewed` (`yes`, `no`). Return only choices matching completed RP. `context_key` follows the current Scene's identity scope. While active, propose once per confirmed source turn; JavaScript judges actual elapsed turns and duplicates. Set `macro_reviewed` to `yes` only when the program-supplied `director_receipt.completed_checks` contains `rhythm.macro_reviewed`.

`rhythm.hook_clock.choices` uses `tier` (`short`, `mid`, `long`), `action` (`plant`, `advance`, `payoff`, `retire`, `extend`), and `stage` (`seeded`, `hinted`, `escalated`, `payoff_ready`, `resolved`, `retired`). Actual evidence and the existing stage must match, and never create several hook actions in one source turn. Propose `extend` only when the source's one-time extension rule applies.

Register a new hook by linking an Event or relevant canonical entry only when it actually appeared in completed RP. Never create a new clue or character that still exists only in a proposal. An unconfirmed next development can attach only to a hook already planted, and it must not be written as a future Event with a confirmed date or Location. When prior `pending` development did not occur, never mark it complete automatically; distinguish whether it remains, changes, or is discarded as a noncanonical adjustment.

Distinguish a payoff condition from what actually appeared. A clue appearing does not establish who noticed it; that requires separate knowledge evidence. Payoff and retirement also change only after an actual result. Never automatically delete the past evidence of a completed item.

Keep the canonical ledger for one hook in one place, and reference it by link from the current Scene or Character. An actual Event requiring date, time, and place follows the base Event format. Never convert source-turn intervals into real time or in-world dates. When no program-supplied ledger time exists, never invent a past turn number.
